Out-of-fold cross-validated predictions (no model is stored)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes out-of-fold cross-validated predictions for a training table without persisting any model. Each row is predicted by a model trained on the other folds (`cv :=` folds, default 5), so the result is an honest, leakage-free prediction per row — ideal for building a held-out prediction column to score with metrics or to stack. Name the label with `target :=`, pick the `estimator :=`, optionally carry an `id :=` through, and tune via JSON `params :=`. Classification labels of any dtype are decoded back to the original values.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated out-of-fold predictions** — no model is stored.

- Each row is predicted by a model fit on the *other* folds (`cv :=`, default 5)
- `estimator :=`, `target :=`, optional `id :=` passthrough, JSON `params :=`
- Returns one `prediction` per input row (label or value), leakage-free

Use it to make a held-out prediction column for metrics or model stacking.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT i.target_name AS actual_species, cv.prediction AS predicted_species, count(*) AS n_flowers FROM xgboost.main.cross_val_predict((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target_name FROM xgboost.main.iris), estimator := 'xgb_classifier', target := 'target_name', id := 'sample_id', cv := 5) AS cv JOIN xgboost.main.iris AS i USING (sample_id) GROUP BY ALL ORDER BY actual_species, predicted_species","description":"Out-of-fold confusion matrix for an XGBoost iris classifier: 5-fold cross_val_predict on the species name, joined back to the iris table by sample_id and counted per (actual, predicted) species pair. Only non-empty cells are returned; the off-diagonal rows are the held-out misclassifications, almost all of them versicolor/virginica mix-ups."},{"sql":"SELECT d.bmi_quartile, count(*) AS patients, round(avg(abs(cv.prediction - d.target)), 1) AS oof_mae, round(avg(d.target), 1) AS mean_progression FROM xgboost.main.cross_val_predict((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.diabetes), estimator := 'xgb_regressor', target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', cv := 5) AS cv JOIN (SELECT sample_id, target, ntile(4) OVER (ORDER BY bmi, sample_id) AS bmi_quartile FROM xgboost.main.diabetes) AS d USING (sample_id) GROUP BY d.bmi_quartile ORDER BY d.bmi_quartile","description":"Where does an XGBoost regressor miss? 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on diabetes joined back to the patients, with the held-out mean absolute error and mean progression score per BMI quartile (1 = lowest BMI)."},{"sql":"SELECT sample_id, prediction FROM xgboost.main.cross_val_predict((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM xgboost.main.iris()), estimator => 'xgb_classifier', target => 'target', id => 'sample_id')","description":"5-fold out-of-fold predictions on iris"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
If `id :=` names a column it is carried through first; the prediction type follows the estimator task.

### Classifier

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| prediction | BIGINT | Out-of-fold class label (`VARCHAR` for string labels). |

### Regressor

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| prediction | DOUBLE | Out-of-fold predicted value. |

Cross-validated held-out scores, one row per fold (no model is stored)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs k-fold cross-validation and returns the held-out score for each fold (one `(fold, score)` row), without storing any model. Name the label with `target :=`, choose the `estimator :=`, set the number of folds with `cv :=` (default 5), and optionally pick a `scoring :=` metric (default: the estimator's own scorer — accuracy for classifiers, R^2 for regressors). Aggregate the rows (e.g. `avg(score)`) for a single cross-validated performance estimate or to compare estimators/hyperparameters.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated fold scores** — one row per fold, no model stored.

- `estimator :=`, `target :=`, `cv :=` folds (default 5), optional `scoring :=`
- Returns `(fold, score)` — the held-out score for each fold

Default scorer is the estimator's own (accuracy / R^2). Take `avg(score)` for a single cross-validated estimate.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT fold, score FROM xgboost.main.cross_val_score((SELECT sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM xgboost.main.iris()), estimator => 'xgb_classifier', target => 'target')","description":"5-fold accuracy of an XGBoost classifier on iris"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "fold", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Cross-validation fold index (0-based)."}, {"name": "score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Held-out score for this fold."}]

Delete a model from the registry

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Deletes a model from the registry by name (`drop_model('my_model')`) and returns one row `(model_name, dropped)` where `dropped` is true when a model was removed and false when the name did not exist. Idempotent and safe to call on an absent model. Use it to clean up models created by `fit`/`fit_<estimator>`/search with a `model_name`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Delete a stored model** — registry cleanup.

- Call positionally: `drop_model('my_model')`
- Returns `(model_name, dropped)`; `dropped` is false if the name did not exist

Idempotent — safe on a missing model.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT model_name, dropped FROM xgboost.main.drop_model('iris_clf')","description":"Delete a stored model and report whether it existed"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "model_name", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Name of the model."}, {"name": "dropped", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "True if a model was deleted, False if it did not exist."}]

rows: Per-row SHAP feature contributions, long format (row, [class], feature, shap_value, base_value)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Streams a table through a stored model and emits SHAP-style per-row prediction contributions (XGBoost's `pred_contribs`) in long format: one row per (input row, feature) with `feature`, `shap_value` (how much that feature pushed this row's raw margin away from the model's base), and `base_value` (the expected margin). Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=` (a `BLOB`); name an `id :=` to tag every emitted row. For multiclass models an extra `class` column appears (one row per (row, class, feature)). Sum `shap_value` over a row's features and add `base_value` to recover the raw margin. Use it for local, per-prediction explanations.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**SHAP explanations** — per-row feature contributions, long format.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; optional `id :=` passthrough
- One row per (input row, feature): `feature`, `shap_value`, `base_value`
- Multiclass adds a `class` `BIGINT` column (one row per (row, class, feature))

`sum(shap_value) + base_value` = the row's raw margin. Local, per-prediction explanation.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT feature, round(avg(abs(shap_value)), 3) AS mean_abs_shap FROM xgboost.main.explain((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.diabetes()), model_name => 'diab_reg', id => 'sample_id') GROUP BY feature ORDER BY mean_abs_shap DESC","description":"Explain each row's prediction with per-feature contributions"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
Long format: one row per (input row, feature). If `id :=` names a column it is carried through first, and multiclass models add a `class` column (one row per input row, class and feature).

### Binary classification or regression

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| feature | VARCHAR | Feature column name. |
| shap_value | DOUBLE | Contribution of the feature to the raw margin. |
| base_value | DOUBLE | Model base (expected) raw-margin value. |

### Multiclass classification

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| class | BIGINT | Class index the contribution is for. |
| feature | VARCHAR | Feature column name. |
| shap_value | DOUBLE | Contribution of the feature to the raw margin for this class. |
| base_value | DOUBLE | Model base (expected) raw-margin value for this class. |

rows: SELECT feature, round(avg(abs(shap_value)), 3) AS mean_abs_shap FROM xgboost.main.explain((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.diabetes()), model_name => 'diab_reg', id => 'sample_id') GROUP BY feature ORDER BY mean_abs_shap DESC
Per-feature importance (weight/gain/cover) for a stored model, ranked

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Returns the booster's built-in per-feature importance for a stored model, one ranked row per feature (`feature`, `importance`, `rank`; rank 1 = most important, already sorted descending). Identify the model positionally by name (`feature_importance('m')`) or with `model :=` (a `BLOB`). Choose the `importance_type :=` — `gain` (default; average loss reduction), `weight` (split count), `cover`, `total_gain`, or `total_cover`. Features never used in a split report importance 0. A fast, model-native ranking; for a model-agnostic alternative use `permutation_importance`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Booster feature importance** — model-native, ranked.

- Identify the model by name (`feature_importance('m')`) or `model :=` `BLOB`
- `importance_type :=` `gain` (default) | `weight` | `cover` | `total_gain` | `total_cover`
- Returns `(feature, importance, rank)`, sorted by importance descending

Unused features score 0. See `permutation_importance` for a model-agnostic measure.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT feature, importance, rank FROM xgboost.main.feature_importance('iris_clf', importance_type => 'gain') WHERE rank <= 3","description":"Top three features by gain for a stored model"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "feature", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Feature column name."}, {"name": "importance", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Importance score for the chosen importance_type."}, {"name": "rank", "type": "INTEGER", "description": "1-based rank by importance (1 = most important)."}]

Fit an XGBoost estimator and store it in the model registry

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Buffers a training table, fits an XGBoost estimator (`estimator :=` one of `xgb_classifier`, `xgb_regressor`, `xgb_rf_classifier`, `xgb_rf_regressor`), and returns a one-row training summary whose `model` column is a self-contained `BLOB` (estimator + metadata). Name the label column with `target :=`; every other column except an optional `id :=` passthrough becomes a feature (strings/missing values handled natively). Hyperparameters go in a JSON `params :=` string. Pass `model_name :=` to also persist the model to the registry; otherwise it lives only in the returned `BLOB`. Feed that `BLOB` to `predict`/`explain`/`feature_importance` via `SET VARIABLE` + `getvariable()`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Fit an XGBoost model** — train and return a reusable model `BLOB`.

- Input: a training table `(SELECT ...)`; name the label with `target :=`, optionally an `id :=` passthrough
- `estimator :=` `xgb_classifier` | `xgb_regressor` | `xgb_rf_classifier` | `xgb_rf_regressor`; hyperparameters via JSON `params :=`
- Returns one row: `estimator`, `task`, `n_samples`/`n_features`/`n_classes`, `train_score`, `features`, and the `model` `BLOB`
- `model_name :=` also persists to the registry; classification labels may be any dtype (string/int/bool) and are decoded back on predict
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT model_name, task, n_samples, n_features, train_score FROM xgboost.main.fit((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM xgboost.main.iris()), model_name => 'iris_clf', estimator => 'xgb_classifier', target => 'target', id => 'sample_id')","description":"Train an XGBoost classifier on iris and store it as 'iris_clf'"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "model_name", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Name the model was stored under ('' if not persisted)."}, {"name": "estimator", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Estimator type used."}, {"name": "task", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "classification or regression."}, {"name": "n_samples", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of training rows."}, {"name": "n_features", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of features."}, {"name": "n_classes", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Number of classes (NULL for regression)."}, {"name": "train_score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "In-sample score (accuracy or R^2)."}, {"name": "features", "type": "VARCHAR[]", "description": "Ordered feature column names."}, {"name": "model", "type": "BLOB", "description": "The fitted model as a self-contained `BLOB` (estimator + metadata)."}]

Fit a xgb_classifier with typed hyperparameters; returns/stores the model

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Buffers a training table and fits a gradient-boosted decision-tree **classifier** (XGBoost's `XGBClassifier`) with its key hyperparameters exposed as typed, named SQL arguments (`n_estimators`, `max_depth`, `learning_rate`, `subsample`, `colsample_bytree`, `min_child_weight`, `gamma`, `reg_alpha`, `reg_lambda`, ...), each defaulting to XGBoost's own documented default. Equivalent to `fit(estimator := 'xgb_classifier', ...)` but discoverable and type-checked in the catalog instead of a JSON `params` blob. Name the classification label with `target :=`, optionally carry an `id :=` through; every other column is a feature (strings/missing values handled natively). Returns the same one-row summary with a reusable `model` `BLOB`, and persists to the registry when `model_name :=` is given. Feed the `BLOB` to `predict`/`explain`/`feature_importance`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**`fit_xgb_classifier`** — fit a gradient-boosted decision-tree **classifier** (XGBoost's `XGBClassifier`) with typed hyperparameters.

- Input: a training table `(SELECT ...)`; name the label with `target :=`, optional `id :=` passthrough
- Hyperparameters are named, typed SQL args (`n_estimators`, `max_depth`, `learning_rate`, `subsample`, `reg_lambda`, ...) at XGBoost's real defaults
- Returns the standard fit summary plus a reusable `model` `BLOB`; `model_name :=` also persists it

The discoverable, type-checked alternative to `fit(estimator := 'xgb_classifier', ...)`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT n_samples, n_features, train_score FROM xgboost.main.fit_xgb_classifier((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.iris()), target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', n_estimators := 200, max_depth := 6)","description":"Train a xgb_classifier with named hyperparameters"}]

Cross-validated grid search over an XGBoost estimator's hyperparameters

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs scikit-learn's `GridSearchCV` over a training table and returns the cross-validation leaderboard — one row per hyperparameter combination tried, with its `params` (JSON), `mean_test_score`, `std_test_score`, and `rank` (1 = best). The estimator and its grid are one tagged-union argument: `estimator := union_value(<estimator> := {param: [values], ...})`, where the union tag picks the estimator and each member exposes only that estimator's hyperparameters; omitted params stay at their default. Set `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `scoring :=`. The refit best model rides as a `model` `BLOB` on the rank-1 row — grab it with `WHERE model IS NOT NULL`; pass `model_name :=` to also persist it.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated grid search** — exhaustive hyperparameter sweep.

- `estimator := union_value(<estimator> := {param: [values], ...})` (a discriminated union; only that estimator's params are exposed)
- `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `scoring :=`, optional `model_name :=`
- Returns the leaderboard: `params`, `mean_test_score`, `std_test_score`, `rank`

The refit best model is a `model` `BLOB` on the rank-1 row — `WHERE model IS NOT NULL`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT params, mean_test_score, rank FROM xgboost.main.grid_search((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.iris()), target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', estimator := union_value(xgb_classifier := {'n_estimators': [50, 100], 'max_depth': [3, 5]})) ORDER BY rank","description":"Grid-search an XGBoost classifier on iris"}]

How a stored model's average prediction changes as one feature varies over a grid

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes the partial-dependence curve for one numeric feature: sweeps `feature :=` over a grid of `grid_resolution :=` points and reports the model's average prediction at each value, holding the rest of the buffered background table fixed. Returns `(feature_value, class, partial_dependence)` ordered along the grid; `class` is NULL for regression and the single binary curve, and is the class index (one curve per class) for multiclass. Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`. Numeric features only (categorical features raise a clear error). Use it to see the marginal effect and shape of a feature on the prediction.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Partial dependence** — marginal effect of one feature.

- `feature :=` (numeric only) swept over `grid_resolution :=` points
- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; input is the background table
- Returns `(feature_value, class, partial_dependence)` along the grid

`class` is NULL for regression/binary, the class index for multiclass (one curve each).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT class, feature_value, partial_dependence FROM xgboost.main.partial_dependence((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', feature := 'petal_length_cm') ORDER BY feature_value","description":"Partial dependence of 'iris_clf' on petal length"}]

Model-agnostic feature importance: the drop in score when each feature is shuffled

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes model-agnostic permutation importance over an evaluation table: for each feature, shuffle its values `n_repeats :=` times and measure the resulting drop in the model's score; a larger drop means a more important feature. Returns one ranked row per feature (`feature`, `importance_mean`, `importance_std`, `rank`; rank 1 = most important). Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`, name the held-out `target :=` column, and optionally set `scoring :=` and `random_state :=`. Unlike `feature_importance` this measures impact on real predictions and respects feature correlations, but it needs labelled data and is slower.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Permutation importance** — model-agnostic, ranked.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; name the `target :=` column
- `n_repeats :=` shuffles per feature, optional `scoring :=`, `random_state :=`
- Returns `(feature, importance_mean, importance_std, rank)`, sorted descending

Measures impact on real predictions (needs labels; slower than `feature_importance`).

Score a table through a stored model, emitting predictions

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Streams a table through an already-fit XGBoost model and emits its predictions. Identify the model with either `model_name :=` (a registry name) or `model :=` (a `BLOB` from `fit`, passed via `SET VARIABLE` + `getvariable()` since a table function has only one subquery slot). Features are matched by name (order-independent; extra columns ignored; missing ones error at bind). The default output is the decoded `prediction` (the original label dtype for classifiers, value for regressors); the mutually exclusive modes `with_proba`, `output_margin`, and `pred_leaf` switch to per-class probabilities, the raw margin, or per-tree leaf indices respectively. Name an `id :=` column to carry it through.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Predict with a stored model** — score a table row by row.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` *or* `model :=` (a `fit` `BLOB`)
- Features aligned by name; an optional `id :=` is carried through
- Default output: `prediction` (label or value)
- `with_proba := true` → one `proba_<class>` column per class; `output_margin := true` → a `margin` `DOUBLE`; `pred_leaf := true` → a `leaf` `INTEGER[]` (one index per tree) — the three modes are mutually exclusive
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT sample_id, prediction FROM xgboost.main.predict((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.iris()), model_name => 'iris_clf', id => 'sample_id')","description":"Predict with the stored 'iris_clf' model"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
If `id :=` names a column it is carried through first. The prediction column depends on the model task and on the prediction mode; `with_proba := true` on a classifier adds one `proba_<class>` `DOUBLE` column per class.

### Classifier (default)

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| prediction | BIGINT | Predicted class label (`VARCHAR` for string labels). |

### Regressor (default)

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| prediction | DOUBLE | Predicted value. |

### output_margin := true

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| margin | DOUBLE | Raw (untransformed) margin score. |

### pred_leaf := true

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sample_id | BIGINT | Column named by `id :=` (here `sample_id`), carried through first as-is. |
| leaf | INTEGER[] | Leaf index reached in each tree, one element per tree. |

Cross-validated randomized search: sample n_iter hyperparameter combinations

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs scikit-learn's `RandomizedSearchCV` over a training table, sampling `n_iter :=` random hyperparameter combinations (capped at the grid size) instead of exhausting the grid — cheaper than `grid_search` for large spaces. Same tagged-union argument: `estimator := union_value(<estimator> := {param: [values], ...})`; omitted params stay at their default. Set `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, `random_state :=` for reproducible sampling, optional `scoring :=`. Returns the same leaderboard (`params`, `mean_test_score`, `std_test_score`, `rank`) with the refit best model as a `model` `BLOB` on the rank-1 row (`WHERE model IS NOT NULL`); `model_name :=` also persists it.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated randomized search** — sample the hyperparameter space.

- `estimator := union_value(<estimator> := {param: [values], ...})` (discriminated union)
- `n_iter :=` combinations to sample (capped at grid size), `random_state :=` for reproducibility
- `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `scoring :=`, optional `model_name :=`

Cheaper than `grid_search` on large grids; best model is a `model` `BLOB` on the rank-1 row.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT params, mean_test_score, rank FROM xgboost.main.randomized_search((SELECT * FROM xgboost.main.iris()), target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', n_iter := 4, estimator := union_value(xgb_classifier := {'n_estimators': [50, 100, 200], 'max_depth': [3, 5, 8]})) ORDER BY rank","description":"Randomized-search an XGBoost classifier on iris"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "estimator", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Estimator that was searched."}, {"name": "params", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "This combination's hyperparameters (JSON)."}, {"name": "mean_test_score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Mean cross-validated score."}, {"name": "std_test_score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Std-dev of the cross-validated score."}, {"name": "rank", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Rank by mean score (1 = best)."}, {"name": "model", "type": "BLOB", "description": "The refit best model as a BLOB (only on the rank-1 row)."}]

Wine recognition dataset (178 samples, 13 features, 3 classes)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Zero-argument table function returning the wine-recognition dataset: 178 rows, one per wine sample, with 13 numeric chemical-analysis features (alcohol, malic acid, ash, magnesium, total phenols, flavanoids, colour intensity, hue, proline, ...), an integer `target` (0/1/2), the cultivar `target_name`, and a `sample_id`. A balanced 3-class dataset over continuous features — handy for multiclass classification demos.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Wine dataset** — 178 wines from three cultivars.

- `sample_id` `INTEGER` — 0-based row index
- 13 `DOUBLE` chemical features (alcohol, phenols, colour intensity, proline, ...)
- `target` `INTEGER` (0–2) and `target_name` the cultivar

Takes no arguments. A continuous-feature 3-class classification benchmark.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"sql":"SELECT target_name, round(avg(alcohol), 2) AS mean_alcohol FROM xgboost.main.wine() GROUP BY target_name ORDER BY target_name","description":"Mean alcohol content per wine cultivar"}]
